messages:
sophia: FYI we got a p99 escalation from AcmePay at ~09:20 PST. error rate normal but tail is awful, customers seeing 2-3x p99 on tokenization endpoint. traces point to long stalls in prefix kv lookups. attaching short trace.
aj: on it. any deploys to us-west in last 4 hours?
kevin: nothing from infra. metrics show a sudden jump in distinct prefix keys for tenant acmepay — went from ~1.8k to ~56k in 12m.
maria: that smells like a header-derived key leak. did they add some per-request header? @support please confirm.
support: confirmed. they rolled out a change that attaches uuid request_id header on every request for tracing. they didn't realize we include headers in prefix key derivation by default.
sophia: ugh. repro steps from support: spawn 1000 concurrent requests each with unique request_id -> p99 spikes. can we reproduce in staging?
aj: repro snippet:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "x-request-id: $RANDOM-$RANDOM" https://staging.redwood/tokenize & done; wait
```
observed p99 jump and kv_miss_rate spiking.
kevin: query I ran:
```
SELECT count(distinct prefix_key) FROM kv_cache WHERE region='us-west' AND tenant='acmepay' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'
```
before: 1.8k, peak: 56.3k. eviction churn up 8x, warmup misses huge.
maria: impact chain: high prefix-cardinality -> eviction churn -> missed kv entries -> longer sequence lengths / extra padding -> more CPU and IO -> tail latency.
sre_lead: short-term: 1) strip noisy headers at ingress for acmepay 2) increase tenant kv max-entries temporarily 3) enable warmup-drip to prefill frequent prefixes 4) consider temporarily routing to compact model if kv miss p99 > threshold for >5m.
ops-bot: starting deploy: feature/ingress-strip-noisy-headers -> us-west-canary
aj: canary applied to us-west-1a. within 90s distinct prefix keys dropped to ~2.9k and p99 returned to baseline. looks correlated.
support: customer rolled back SDK change after we asked; they reported latency normalized. they still want us to be resilient if other customers send noisy headers.
kevin: follow-ups (owner tags):
- telemetry: add per-tenant "header-derived-key-entropy" metric and alert when > X (kevin)
- runtime: default-to-normalize header-based prefix keys and whitelist low-cardinality headers (maria)
- policy: when tenant prefix key cardinality > Y, auto-enable LFU eviction + warmup-drip + ingress normalization (sre_lead)
- docs: notify customers about header hygiene and SDK guidance (support)
maria: also propose a runtime safeguard: if we detect >N unique prefix keys in sliding 10m window, flip a soft circuit that treats headers as non-keyed until stabilized, and tag requests for postmortem.
sophia: good. let's schedule a short postmortem doc and a follow-up in eng-runtime channel with next steps. add a quick playbook entry to incidents/playbooks/kv-cardinality.json.
aj: I'll push the telemetry dashboards and add an alert with a 3m eval window.
kevin: one more note — we should avoid increasing kv max-entries as routine; it's fine as hotfix but not a long-term mitigation.
sre_lead: agreed. long-term we want normalization + auto-policy + customer docs. I'll own the incident writeup. closing here.
